subject: Media Literacy
title: Algorithmic Radicalization
description: A short lesson to help you apply Algorithmic Radicalization.

hook.text: A teen watches one fitness video. YouTube recommends extreme dieting. Then eating disorders. In three hours.

buildup.text: Recommendation algorithms push increasingly extreme content because extreme content gets more engagement.

discovery.text: Researchers found YouTube's recommendations systematically led users from mainstream to extremist content.

twist.text: The algorithm isn't promoting extremism intentionally. It's optimizing for watch time, and extreme content delivers.

climax.text: Radicalization isn't a bug in the algorithm. It's a side effect of optimizing for engagement at all costs.

punchline.text: The algorithm doesn't want you radical. It wants you watching.

quiz.question: Why do recommendation algorithms push increasingly extreme content?
options: Extreme content gets more engagement, which the algorithm optimizes for
